text: lets tackle the parts of this that are immediate wins, like specifically the physics rects on exported props, build a plan to execute on. if you have questions, do not ask me them through the harness question interface, it tends to be opinionated in the wrong direction and i have the opinions. @cart/editor/FLOCKBOOK_DESIGN.md
resolution: Executed FLOCKBOOK_DESIGN §10's standalone quick win (the physics-rects-on-exported-props item). Exploration first confirmed the runtime is already triangles-final since req_3329 (boxes demoted to broadphase via EXACT_MESH_COARSE_SOLID_FLAG; player contact resolves in mesh_collision.zig) — the real gap was that the collision bake was never persisted: compileOutlinerCollision ran only transiently at live push, no package on disk carried collision, and all four save/export paths skipped it. Built the persistence: RJCB v1 codec (encode/decodeCollisionBake in model/meshCollision.ts, strict null-on-damage decode), writePackageCollision in modelPackageStore (placeable-frame bake over ground-rebased doc verts, doc-revision stamped, stamp-gated idempotent), wired into writeModelArtifacts (every save branch incl. paint-only self-heal) and materializePackageArtifacts (GLB/OBJ import bakes at arrival). groundRebase moved to model/groundRebase.ts to break the import cycle (authoredMesh re-exports). residentMeshFor deliberately keeps baking live from rendered verts — the surface that stops you is the surface drawn; the blob is the package's durable declaration for folder consumers. Backfilled all 137 existing packages headlessly (v8cli script; 3 file-backed .glb/.obj packages correctly decline — no JS-readable geometry), verified idempotent on second run, 7/7 meshCollision tests pass incl. 3 new codec tests. Docs + index record updated in the same commit.
